Neither shows current effect, and neither is used as a basis. I searched the held corpus for the order's number (only the order's own Federal Register text and the 1989 codification entry cite it), read the three bounded machine searches (current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr with no hit that ends it, later-events:ofr_catalog with no later event), and read the order's own terms (a single delegation with no date, event or condition that ends it). notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: Executive Order 11874 (July 25, 1975; 40 FR 31737) is a single delegation to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget of the President's authority under section 1012 of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964, as amended by the Legal Services Corporation Act of 1974 (42 U.S.C. 2996k), to direct that appropriate support functions of the Federal Government may be made available to the Legal Services Corporation. The held original has no own-terms end. No held later order, statute or regulation amends, revokes or supersedes it. The United States Code (release point 119-121, printed through 2026-10-09) prints the order in full as a note under 42 U.S.C. 2996k without an ending statement. Coverage gap: laws enacted 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that release, and no held source suggests any touches the order. Recommended provisional status: yes.
